title: Inhaled Treprostinil Response Assessed by Hyperpolarized 129Xe MRI in Adults With Pulmonary Hypertension Associated With Interstitial Lung Disease (X-TRIPP)
official: Assessing Acute Pharmacodynamics and Long-Term Response to Inhaled Prostacyclin With Hyperpolarized 129Xe MRI in Patients With PH-ILD (X-TRIPP)
summary: This prospective multicenter study will evaluate adults with pulmonary hypertension associated with interstitial lung disease (PH-ILD) who are newly prescribed standard-of-care inhaled treprostinil. Hyperpolarized 129Xe MRI will be performed before treatment and after 12 weeks to assess changes in lung gas transfer, including red blood cell (RBC) defect percentage. At 12 weeks, MRI will also be performed before and after a dose of inhaled treprostinil to characterize acute effects. The study will examine whether changes in 129Xe MRI measures are associated with treatment response, including changes in six-minute walk distance, pulmonary function, and plasma BNP levels.
conditions: Pulmonary Hypertension Associated With Interstitial Lung Disease
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria

* Patients aged ≥18 with a confirmed diagnosis of WHO Group 3 PH based on CT imaging
* Right heart catheterization within 1 year prior to baseline study visit, with the following documented parameters:

  * Pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR) \>3 WU
  * Pulmonary capillary wedge pressure (PCWP) of ≤15 mm Hg
  * Mean pulmonary arterial pressure (mPAP) of ≥20 mm Hg
* Baseline 6MWD ≥100 m
* A stable and optimized dose for ≥30 days prior to initiation of treatment with inhaled treprostinil on a chronic medication for underlying lung disease (ie, pirfenidone, nintedanib)

Exclusion Criteria

* Diagnosis of PAH or PH for reasons other than WHO Group 3 PH-ILD
* Patients with Combined Pulmonary Fibrosis and Emphysema (CPFE)
* Received any PAH-approved therapy within 60 days of initiation of treatment with inhaled treprostinil
* Evidence of clinically significant left-sided heart disease (PCWP \>15 mm Hg and LVEF \<40%)
* Received \>10 L/min oxygen supplementation by any mode of delivery at baseline
* Exacerbation of underlying lung disease or active pulmonary or upper respiratory infection within 30 days of initiation of treatment with inhaled treprostinil
* Initiation of pulmonary rehabilitation within 12 weeks prior to initiation of treatment with inhaled treprostinil
* Acute pulmonary embolism within 90 days of initiation of treatment with inhaled treprostinil
* Any contraindication to subject receiving a MRI, per investigator discretion
* Pregnancy
